turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung protested that he did not want to hear such talk, that O-lan's condition was already too grave to be thinking of such things, and that he wanted her to rest and recover.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told O-lan that he would marry the maid, as she had always wished, and that he would make her happy in the house, and that she could rest easy knowing that he and his wife would take care of her and his father.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: the maid asked, in a barely audible voice, if the eldest son was really certain he wanted to marry her, and if O-lan was truly content with the thought of their marriage

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan asked the eldest son if he was certain he wanted to marry the maid, and what would happen to her and Wang Lung when she was gone

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she must not worry about such things, that he and the eldest son would take care of her and their home, and that she must focus on recovering

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told O-lan and Wang Lung that he would do everything in his power to make his mother happy and ensure the family's well-being, and that he would not let them down.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: the maid looked down, her voice barely above a whisper, as she asked O-lan if she thought she would be a good wife for the eldest son, and if she could make him happy

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan looked at the eldest son and the maid, her eyes filled with a deep concern, and asked if they were truly certain of each other, and if they were prepared for the responsibilities that marriage would bring

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that he would not lose her, that she would recover and be with them again, and that they would face the future together

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told O-lan that he trusted her judgment and was confident that she had chosen a kind and hardworking wife for him, and that he would do his best to make her happy.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid looked down, her voice barely above a whisper, as she told O-lan that she would do her best to be a good wife to the eldest son and bring honor to their family.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told the eldest son and the maid that she was glad they were making such a commitment to each other, and that she would do everything in her power to ensure their happiness

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung insisted that O-lan must not exhaust herself with these concerns, that her health was the only thing that mattered, and that he would take care of everything

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son reassured his mother that she must not worry about him and his new wife, that he and the maid would manage well on their own, and that she should focus on getting better.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid looked down, her voice barely above a whisper, as she asked O-lan if there was anything she could do to help with her motherly duties, wanting to ease her burden.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan looked at Wang Lung with a hint of sadness in her eyes and told him that she could not help but worry about the future, for she had seen the hardships that life had brought to their family and she wanted to ensure that her son and his new wife would not suffer as she had.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that he would not let her burden herself with such worries, that he would work day and night to ensure their son's future was secure.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told his mother that he would work alongside his father to ensure the family's prosperity and take some of the burden off Wang Lung's shoulders.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid told O-lan that she would like to help with the household chores and take some of the burden off her shoulders, so that she could focus on resting and getting better.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan turned to Wang Lung and told him that she had seen the good life of the wealthy families in the city and wished for her son to have the same opportunities, but now it seemed that this might not be possible.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that there was another thing she had to attend to before she could die.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung insisted that O-lan should not speak of dying and that it would please him if she did not.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan replied that she had to die, for she felt it in her vitals waiting, but she would not die before her eldest son came home and before he wedded this good maid who was her daughter-in-law, and well she served O-lan, holding the hot water basin steadily and knowing when to bathe O-lan's face when she sweated in pain. Now O-lan wanted her son to come home, because she had to die, and she wanted him to wed this maid first, so that she might die easily, knowing that her grandson was stirred into life and a great-grandson for the old one.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she looked twice as well as they had said and years away from death.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan declared that she would see Wang Lung wedded and then she must die.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan instructed Wang Lung to sit there and drink the wine and eat the rice of his marriage, for she would see it all and this would be his bed of marriage since she was soon to be finished with it and carried away.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan asked if everyone had wine, if the sweet rice dish in the middle of the feast was very hot, if they had put full measure of lard and sugar into it, and if the eight fruits were present.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she was now content and that this thing in her may do as it would. She instructed her son to look to his father and his grandfather, and her daughter to look to her husband and his father and his grandfather and the poor fool in the court, there she was. And she told Wang Lung that he had no duty to any other.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan said that, even if she was ugly, she had borne a son; although she was but a slave, there was a son in her house.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan insisted that no one else could feed Wang Lung's son and care for him as she did. She told Wang Lung that beauty would not bear a man sons.
